sources.title: Ling-3.0-flash official model card
sources.evidence: Exact text model: MIT, nominal 124B total/5.1B active, 35 KDA plus 7 gated MLA layers, two dense FFN layers, 512 routed experts with 8 selected and one shared expert. Documents thinking, tools, and 256K serving.

sources.title: Ling-3.0-flash checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM; 42 backbone layers; one next-token-prediction layer; 512 routed experts, top-8, one shared; max_position_embeddings=262144; tie_word_embeddings=false; BF16 checkpoint.

sources.title: Ling-3.0-flash official model implementation
sources.evidence: Defines 42 hybrid KDA/MLA backbone layers plus MTP at layer 42; sigmoid group-limited top-8 routing (4 selected groups of 8), one shared expert, expert_bias registered as a buffer. Input embedding and output head are separate; MTP reuses them. KDA A_log and dt_bias are learned parameters.

sources.title: Ling-3.0-flash complete checkpoint weight index
sources.evidence: Indexes 63,783 named tensors across 24 shards. All indexed names matched the bounded shard headers; includes auxiliary MTP layer 42.

sources.title: Ling-3.0-flash BF16 checkpoint tensor headers, all 24 shards
sources.evidence: Read only bytes 0-7 and each JSON header from model-00001-of-00024.safetensors through model-00024-of-00024.safetensors, with HTTP 206 and Content-Range checks. Shapes sum to 127,486,405,600 elements. Removing 41 expert_bias buffers of 512 elements yields 127,486,384,608 learned parameters; no quantization metadata. Backbone: 124,414,191,072; MTP: 3,072,193,536. No duplicated names or tied embedding/head alias is counted.

sources.title: Ling-3.0-flash official chat template
sources.evidence: Text conversation template supports enable_thinking, tool definitions, assistant tool_calls and tool responses.

sources.title: Ant Ling platform release changelog
sources.evidence: Official changelog directly fetched successfully (HTTP 200) at the exact /en/docs/getting-started/changelog/ URL. Under July 23, 2026 and v2.0.0 it states: "Launched the all-new cost-effective Ling-3.0-flash model." The surrounding entry documents chat/API availability and thinking toggles. This is the initial public release, preceding the weight upload.

sources.title: Official Ling model family and comparison table
sources.evidence: Identifies Ling as Ant Group's MoE model series. Exact Ling-3.0-flash row gives 124B/5.1B and 256K; its detailed section explicitly advertises native 256K context extendable up to 1M. VL, tiny and 3.1 are separate entries. No precise 1M token integer or extension recipe is specified here.

sources.title: Official Ling-3.0 training-checkpoint documentation
sources.evidence: Links the post-trained Ling-3.0-flash separately from base training stages and labels the 5.1B figure Non-emb. This related base-card label does not explicitly define whether input embedding, output head or MTP is excluded. No exact-model counting convention is transferred from it.

sources.title: Ling-3.0-flash: More Useful Work per Token
sources.evidence: Official July 24, 2026 release article advertises native 256K context extendable to 1M for exact Ling-3.0-flash; it does not publish a precise extended token cap, scaling recipe or long-context evaluation at 1M.

sources.title: SGLang exact-model Ling-3.0-flash deployment cookbook
sources.evidence: Deployment cookbook linked by the model publisher states native context is 256K and reads max_position_embeddings from the checkpoint. The current page provides no 1M extension recipe or evaluation; examined its complete Markdown version as well.

sources.title: vLLM exact-model Ling-3.0-flash deployment recipe
sources.evidence: Exact-model prerequisites specify 262144 context, and an MI300X BF16 run documents serving that full context. No 1M recipe or test is reported in this model's page.

name.note: Display spelling of the exact Ling-3.0-flash model, without Fin, Sante, VL, Preview or Plus suffixes.

developer.note: Published by the official inclusionAI organization; Ant Ling documentation identifies Ant Group as the developer organization.

family.note: Normalized name for the officially documented Ling family.

release_date.note: Explicit initial public chat/API launch. The later checkpoint upload is not the first release.

open_weights.note: Official checkpoint is publicly accessible; all 24 shard headers were read without authentication.

license.note: Exact model card license metadata declares MIT.

parameters_b.note: Complete unquantized checkpoint count in decimal billions, including the auxiliary MTP layer. 127,486,405,600 stored elements minus 20,992 non-parameter routing-buffer elements. Input and output embeddings are untied; MTP reuses them without duplicate tensors. The advertised 124B refers to the 124.414191072B backbone, excluding the 3.072193536B MTP component.

active_parameters_b.note: 5.1B is the exact model's published nominal activation figure; the developer does not fully define its accounting scope. A related base card says Non-emb without defining exclusions. Independently, top-8 accounting on the audited backbone gives 5.505672672B when both full embedding/head matrices are included, or 5.103281632B when the input embedding alone is removed. The latter rounds to 5.1B but is arithmetic inference, not proof of the developer's convention; no input-only exclusion or MTP scope is asserted.

architecture.note: Hybrid-linear causal language model: 35 KDA and 7 gated MLA layers in a 5:1 pattern, first two dense FFNs, then 40 MoE FFNs; each has 512 routed experts, top-8 selection plus one shared expert. One additional MLA/MoE MTP layer is in the checkpoint. Routing applies sigmoid scores, selects four of eight groups, then eight experts.

context_window.note: Catalog maximum represented as the developer's advertised 1M extension, using nominal decimal notation (1000000), not an inferred exact 1048576-token cap. Native/configured and documented deployment context is 262144; model-card evaluations use 256K. Neither the examined developer pages nor the linked SGLang/vLLM recipes supplies an exact-model 1M scaling recipe or evaluation. Thus 1M is an advertised extension capability, not a verified endpoint limit or empirical validation.

modalities.note: Exact causal text checkpoint and template; the visually capable Ling-3.0-flash-VL is a separate model.

reasoning.note: Supports selectable thinking mode; enabled by default in the published template.

tool_call.note: Published template formats supplied tools, assistant function calls and tool responses.

description.value: Text-only hybrid-linear MoE model with a 42-layer KDA/MLA backbone, top-8 routing among 512 experts plus one shared expert, optional thinking, and tool use.
description.note: Replaces ambiguous nominal-total wording with concrete architecture and supported capabilities; no unverified efficiency or benchmark claim.

patch.description: Text-only hybrid-linear MoE model with a 42-layer KDA/MLA backbone, top-8 routing among 512 experts plus one shared expert, optional thinking, and tool use.
patch.notes: Complete checkpoint: 127.486384608B learned parameters = 124.414191072B backbone + 3.072193536B auxiliary MTP; excludes 20,992 routing-buffer elements. Official 124B is a nominal backbone count. Official 5.1B active is nominal; its exact accounting scope is not defined. Excluding only the input embedding produces a matching rounded figure but is an inference. Context: advertised extension up to 1M (nominal), versus 262144 native/configured and documented in deployment recipes; an exact 1M cap, extension recipe and evaluation were not established. MIT weights followed the July 23, 2026 chat/API launch.

summary: All 14 published factual fields assessed. Complete learned checkpoint count is 127.486384608B, including MTP and excluding routing buffers; official 5.1B active remains nominal with undefined scope. Exact input-only embedding exclusion is labeled as inference and no active scope is proposed. Set context to the nominal advertised 1M extension while retaining 262144 native/configured and recipe context in notes; no exact 1M recipe/evaluation was established. Directly fetched official changelog confirms July 23, 2026. MIT, public weights, text-only I/O, thinking and tool use are supported.
